ASV ends the verse at 'in this confidence' with nothing for τῆς καυχήσεως; the longer reading would have produced 'this confident boasting' or 'this confidence of glorying', and ASV elsewhere renders καύχησις explicitly.

The ASV compresses houtos hos into the single *as*, which the comparative particle carries, as EPH.5.33 gives *as* to hos and only the extra *even* to houtos; here nothing is left over. A reading giving *as* to the adverb instead is defensible, and this is the corpus's first unrealized houtos.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'go before unto you' renders either preposition with ὑμᾶς identically; εἰς and πρός are indistinguishable in this English, and the verse's two notes concern 'bounty' and 'extortion', not this unit.
ASV 'aforepromised bounty' renders a compound of ἐπαγγέλλομαι (promise); προκατηγγελμένην, from καταγγέλλω, would have given a prior announcing or notice rather than a promise.

Rule 45: *bountifully* realizes epi nowhere, so the pair is one noncompositional unit headed on the governed noun. Rule 35's aligned contrast needs the English to spell the preposition in, as *wherewith* and *thereunto* do; an adverbial -ly does not. 2CO.7.10 settles it, making *godly* noncompositional for kata theon even though *god-ly* carries the noun's own gloss. Reading the pair as aligned is the competing analysis.
The doubled prepositional phrase: the second pair takes the second *bountifully*, with the reaping clause; analysed as the first pair (rule 45, after 2CO.7.10).

The main clause is verbless in Greek; under rule 56 the subject is the only token left to carry the supplied 'Let ... do', and 'man' is a generic completion of 'each' (rule 17), so the head stays on 'each'.
'according as' is one clause-introducer for the comparative adverb; headed on 'as', the lexeme's own gloss, not on the first word (rule 17).
No genitive pronoun competes for the determiner slot, so the supplied possessive is the article's own under rule 20, with the case preposition riding along under rule 21.

variant_decisions.evidence: ASV 'seed to the sower' translates σπόρον and σπέρμα alike; both are rendered 'seed' and the English gives no feature separating them.
ASV reads 'shall supply', a future indicative statement, matching χορηγήσει; the aorist optative χορηγήσαι would have been rendered as a wish, 'may he supply'.
ASV 'shall supply and multiply your seed' carries the future indicative through to this verb, matching πληθυνεῖ rather than the optative πληθύναι ('may he multiply').
ASV 'and increase the fruits of your righteousness' continues the same future indicative construction, matching αὐξήσει; the optative αὐξήσαι would have given 'and may he increase'.

Periphrastic estin + participle rendered by the simple finite verbs *filleth up* and *aboundeth*; the ASV writes no separate auxiliary, so the copula has no token of its own (rule 23's principle for a verb). Aligning it to *filleth* is not available: rule 1 partitions that token to the participle, and merging the pair would need *filleth up* to carry part of estin, which rule 35's test denies. 2CO.8.22 leaves a collapsed copula unrepresented the same way; GAL.2.11 is the contrast, where the ASV supplied a spare verb for it to take.
